sections.h2: Which office handles an Odessa tax account
sections.html:
A single Odessa account can fund many units at once, and the Ector County Appraisal District is the first office to call. Active taxing units around Odessa include the City of Odessa, Ector County, Ector County ISD, the Odessa Junior College District, a county hospital district, a utility district and two emergency service districts.

Ector County's assessor-collector office does not take property tax payments. Instead the appraisal district both appraises and collects, and it answers questions about what you owe at 432-332-6834. Its office is at 1301 E. 8th St. in Odessa.

Part of Odessa extends into Midland County, and the city itself sets no values in either county. Before searching for an account or filing a protest, confirm which district has your parcel.

For 2026-27 the city's taxpayer impact statement shows $0.471578 per $100 of valuation, a hair above the prior year's $0.470700. City property tax pays for firefighters, police officers, road repairs and parks.

The city's slice is modest. School, county, college and hospital districts, plus any special district, each levy a separate rate on the same parcel. Property tax supplies 15.8 percent of city revenue and sales tax 18.2 percent. The city's piece of sales tax is 1.25 percent of the 8.25 percent total.

Treat January 31 as a cliff. Statements arrive in the fall and the account stays clean through the end of January. Starting February 1 the collector adds charges, and they keep growing through the summer.

  • February 1: the unpaid balance takes on six percent in penalty plus one percent in interest.
  • Every month after: the penalty gains a point until July, when it is twelve percent. Interest never stops at that one percent a month.
  • A taxing unit with a delinquent-tax lawyer under contract may add as much as one fifth of the balance.
  • Paying in halves is allowed: the first by the end of November, the second by the end of June.

Older or disabled homestead owners have a four-payment path. A homestead owner already behind may ask for a longer plan, and a few collectors go as far as 36 months. To have penalty and interest forgiven, pay the tax within three weeks of learning about the problem and send the written request before day 181.

sections.h2: Homestead exemptions and the growth cap
sections.html:
The homestead exemption comes first. A 2026 sheet from the appraisal district, Exemption Amounts by Entity, shows what each Odessa-area unit gives, the city, the county and the college among them.

  • School tax: $140,000 of a homestead's value is exempt.
  • Seniors and disabled owners: a further $60,000 comes off school tax. Taking the senior break replaces the disabled one.
  • Optional breaks: a taxing unit can adopt a percentage up to 20 percent, with a $5,000 floor.
  • Growth limit: after the exemption begins, appraised value is held to a 10 percent annual rise.
  • Freeze: seniors and disabled owners generally lock the school levy at the first qualifying year's amount.

Applications go to the appraisal district before May 1. If you buy after New Year's Day and the previous owner never claimed, you can still file for the remainder of that year. A disabled veteran gets a sliding exemption tied to the VA rating that tops out at $12,000, and a 100 percent rating means no tax on the residence homestead.

Protests are due May 15, or 30 days after you receive the notice if that is later. Read the property description on the notice line by line before the hearing.

An owner still unhappy after the review board hearing can sue in district court, ask for binding arbitration, or go before the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the disputed value tops $1,000,000.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax when an Odessa house is sold
sections.html:
Each January 1 a lien is born, and it travels with the house. Delinquent amounts block clear title for a buyer, while the person who owned on that January 1 can still be pursued for the year's bill. The settlement sheet will show the current year prorated by the title company.

If delinquent tax ends in a tax foreclosure sale, a former homestead owner has two years after the buyer's deed is filed to buy the property back, and other property has 180 days. The buy-back price carries a premium over the bid. Leftover sale money can be claimed by the prior owner, but only for 24 months.

A few city rules reach a seller before listing. Residential building permits come from the Building Inspection division at 411 W. 8th Street, by phone at 432-335-3214 or through the online portal. If the city engineer calls a sidewalk, driveway or curb hazardous, the adjoining owner has 30 days from notice to fix it. Owners of rentals must keep working smoke detectors in each unit.

sections.h2: Selling an Odessa house that owes back tax
sections.html:
Back tax rarely stops a sale. Get a payoff from the appraisal district that separates tax, penalty and interest by year, and hand it to the title company before you accept any offer. The title company settles the balance from the buyer's money at closing and you keep the rest.

Bring to the closing office your latest statement, your account number, the appraisal district's contact details and proof of any exemption on the house. If you inherited the property, sort out who may sign a deed before you list, because the title company will ask. Also check whether any sidewalk, driveway or curb notice from the city is still open.

A cash buyer closes without waiting for a lender's appraisal, which helps when penalties are growing each month. The payoff still gets cleared at the table. Before you list, also gather the Building Inspection permit history for any past work, since an open permit question can slow a closing.

Odessa had 99,940 residents in 2010 and 114,428 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 122,707, about 7.2 percent above the 2020 base. Owners occupy 59.8 percent of homes. The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $223,100, renters pay $1,315 at the median and median household income is $73,472. Those are citywide midpoints, so your own appraisal sets your own bill.

faqs.q: Is Odessa property tax due on January 31?
faqs.a: Yes, it is the last clean day. Charges start on February 1, and the penalty alone is twelve percent by July.

faqs.q: Where does an Odessa owner send the tax payment?
faqs.a: Start with the Ector County Appraisal District at 432-332-6834. The county's assessor-collector does not collect, and the district may. A Midland County parcel follows that county's district.

faqs.q: What is the Odessa city tax rate for 2026-27?
faqs.a: The city statement shows $0.471578 for every $100 of valuation. School, county, college and special-district rates come on top.

faqs.q: Does Odessa have its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Ask the appraisal district for its 2026 Exemption Amounts by Entity sheet, which names the amount each unit grants, the City of Odessa included. State law fixes only the school district break at $140,000.

faqs.q: What if I sell an Odessa house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: It is usually paid from the sale proceeds at the closing table, since the lien stays with the lot. The January 1 owner also remains liable for that year.
